qs.q: Which muscle serves as the landmark that divides the posterior triangle of the neck into the occipital and subclavian triangles?
qs.e: The posterior triangle of the neck is subdivided into the upper occipital triangle and lower subclavian triangle by the inferior belly of the omohyoid muscle. The sternocleidomastoid and trapezius form the anterior and posterior boundaries of the entire triangle, respectively.

qs.q: While reviewing the boundaries of the posterior triangle of the neck for a surgical anatomy review, a resident notes the structure that subdivides it into the occipital and subclavian triangles. What is this structure?
qs.e: The inferior belly of the omohyoid muscle divides the posterior triangle into the occipital and subclavian triangles. The other muscles form the overall boundaries or different regions.

qs.q: Which muscle forms the posterior boundary of the posterior triangle of the neck?
qs.e: The posterior triangle of the neck is bounded anteriorly by the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, posteriorly by the anterior border of the trapezius, and inferiorly by the middle third of the clavicle. The inferior belly of the omohyoid muscle crosses it.
